ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-07-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Patel, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Fever, headache, and neck stiffness

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 20-year-old male with allergic rhinitis, acne, and prior meningitis (1/2020, 7/2020) presents with a 2-day history of fever, headache, and neck stiffness. He also reports a non-pruritic rash that started on his trunk and spread to his extremities. His roommate was recently diagnosed with bacterial meningitis.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Meningococcal meningitis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Acute bacterial meningitis (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis
- Acne vulgaris

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Wisdom teeth extraction (age 17)
- Tonsillectomy (age 6)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Cetirizine 10 mg PO daily PRN
- Adapalene 0.1% gel Apply to face nightly

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal first cousin with meningococcal disease requiring hospitalization (childhood)
- Paternal grandmother with rheumatoid arthritis
- Father with hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Social (weekend use, heavier consumption during recent spring break trip). Occupation: Undergraduate college student (sophomore, residing in campus dormitory).

VITAL SIGNS:
On examination, the patient is febrile with a temperature of 39.2°C (102.6°F), heart rate of 110 bpm, and blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
He has a petechial rash with some areas coalescing into purpura. Neurological examination reveals nuchal rigidity.

LABORATORY DATA:
Initial laboratory tests reveal:

- WBC count: 15,000/µL
- Hemoglobin: 13.5 g/dL
- Platelet count: 50,000/µL
- Prothrombin time (PT): 18 seconds (normal: 11-13.5 seconds)
- Partial thromboplastin time (PTT): 45 seconds (normal: 25-35 seconds)
- Fibrinogen: 150 mg/dL (normal: 200-400 mg/dL)
